# Adjudication Task — Chapter 726

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃726화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [동기화]를 시작합니다.
 10|
 11|- 10, 9, 8, 7, 6…….
 12|
 13|- [로그아웃]을 완료했습니다.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|익숙한 종소리와 함께 눈을 떴다. 까마득히 높은 천장이 가장 먼저 시야에 들어온다.
 18|
 19|낡고 마른 풀 냄새가 풍기는 목제 천장이 아닌, 단단한 합금으로 이루어진 새하얀 천장.
 20|
 21|도무지 익숙해지지 않는 그 괴리감 속에서, 나는 현대에서의 마지막 기억을 떠올렸다.
 22|
 23|‘트레이닝 룸.’
 24|
 25|맞다. 여긴 나를 포함한 극소수의 인물만이 드나들 수 있는 평화 길드의 트레이닝 룸이다.
 26|
 27|뛰어난 보안 시설과 경계 시스템을 갖춘 이곳에서 나는 무림으로 떠났다.
 28|
 29|고민 끝에 미뤄 두었던 어떤 중요한 일을 끝끝내 마무리 지은 직후에.
 30|
 31|‘그래, 그랬지.’
 32|
 33|나는 말 없이 천장을 바라보았다.
 34|
 35|이미 지난 날의 기억도, 감각도 돌아온 상황. 그러나 당장 몸을 일으킬 의욕은 눈곱만큼도 들지 않았다.
 36|
 37|무림과 현대. 현대와 무림.
 38|
 39|두 세상을 오갈 때마다 잠시 무기력함에 빠지는 건 내게 있어 그리 드문 일이 아니었지만, 이번에는 특히나 그랬다.
 40|
 41|‘……이걸 질러 버렸네.’
 42|
 43|내 비밀을 누군가에게 알린다면 어떨까, 라는 상상은 지금까지 수십 번도 넘게 해 봤다.
 44|
 45|물론 그 상상을 실행에 옮긴 적은 단 한 번도 없었고, 그래서도 안 됐다.
 46|
 47|‘너무 큰 위험을 동반하는 일이었으니까.’
 48|
 49|하지만…… 한편으로는 어렴풋이 이런 날이 오리라는 생각을 품고 있던 것도 사실이다.
 50|
 51|다만 먼 미래처럼 느껴지던 그 날이, 바로 오늘이 될 줄은 몰랐다.
 52|
 53|
 54|
 55|‘뭐라?’
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|처음 내 고백을 들었을 때, 적천강이 보였던 반응이 아직도 눈앞에 선하다.
 60|
 61|그는 경악이나 황당하다는 기색을 보이지 않았다. 아니, 이해 자체를 하지 못했다.
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|‘지금, 뭐라 했느냐?’
 66|
 67|‘말씀드린 그대로입니다. 제가 그, 노야가 생각하시는 것보다 먼 곳에서 왔거든요.’
 68|
 69|‘산서성이 중원에서 좀 멀긴 하지. 그런데 그게 네놈의 비밀과 무슨 상관이…….’
 70|
 71|‘더 멀어요. 심지어 남만보다도 더.’
 72|
 73|‘남만보다 더?’
 74|
 75|‘예. 평생 걸어도 닿을 수 없을 만큼.’
 76|
 77|‘배를 타고 가야 한다는 말이냐?’
 78|
 79|‘아뇨. 그런 개념이 아니에요. 그러니까…… 완전히 다른 세상이라고 하는 게 맞겠네요.’
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|완전히 다른 세상.
 84|
 85|그리고 이어지는 이야기를 들은 적천강은 한참을 침묵했고, 자신만의 방식으로 내 말을 이해하려 애썼다.
 86|
 87|
 88|
 89|‘말인즉슨, 네 녀석이 선계(仙界)에서 왔다는 소리로구나.’
 90|
 91|‘……어. 글쎄요. 그게 그렇게 되나.’
 92|
 93|‘소신선이냐?’
 94|
 95|‘소시민인데요.’
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|아마 적천강이 현대인이었다면 어느 정도는 말이 통했을 것이다.
100|
101|이미 몬스터와 마법이 존재하는 세상에 무림인 하나 끼어든다고 해서 이해하지 못할 상황은 아니었으니까.
102|
103|물론 그 후에 정신병원으로 가느냐, 실험실로 끌려가느냐는 나중 문제다.
104|
105|하지만 인터넷도 없는 무림에서 장장 백 년을 넘게 살아온 적천강의 귀에는, 내가 하는 모든 이야기들이 혼란스럽게만 들릴 수밖에 없었다.
106|
107|
108|
109|‘이곳에서 잠에 들면 선계로 간다?’
110|
111|‘매번 그런 것은 아니지만, 특수한 상황을 제외하면 그렇습니다.’
112|
113|‘하면 네 녀석이 선계에 머무르다 돌아오려 할 때는.’
114|
115|‘똑같아요. 그럴 때마다 또 다른 세상의 시간은 매우 느리게 흘러가고요.’
116|
117|‘……염병할.’
118|
119|
120|
121|그리고 상식과 이성을 양손에 부여잡고 벌인 악전고투 끝에, 적천강은 마침내 한 가지 결론에 도달했다.
122|
123|
124|
125|‘빌어먹을. 모르겠다.’
126|
127|‘예?’
128|
129|‘아무리 들어도 모르겠단 말이다.’
130|
131|
132|
133|세상에는 두 눈으로 보고, 두 귀로 들어도 이해할 수 없는 진실이 존재한다.
134|
135|적천강에게는 내게 들은 모든 이야기가 그러했고, 이러한 혼란 속에서도 변함없는 사실 역시 있었다.
136|
137|
138|
139|‘하지만 지금 노부가 바라보고 있는 어느 멍청한 놈의 이름은 진태경이지. 선계에서 내려온 소신선이 아닌, 열화신룡 진태경.’
140|
141|‘……!’
142|
143|‘단지 그것만으로 족하다.’
144|
145|
146|
147|그때는 몰랐다.
148|
149|그 한마디를 듣는 순간. 왜 나도 모르게 말문이 막혔는지. 가슴 속에서 울컥 솟구치는 뜨거운 무언가를 참기 위해 이를 악물어야 했는지.
150|
151|하지만…… 그래, 적천강의 말처럼 나 역시 그것만으로 족했다.
152|
153|그리고 이제는 어렴풋이 알 것 같았다.
154|
155|나는 두려웠던 거다. 이미 삶의 일부가 되어 버린 또 다른 세상 속, 내 존재가 부정당하는 것이 무서웠던 거다.
156|
157|‘이건 뭐, 어린애도 아니고.’
158|
159|괜한 헛웃음이 흘러나온다. 동시에 마음 한구석을 짓누르던 바위가 사라지고, 모든 것이 후련하게만 느껴졌다.
160|
161|‘그래, 이걸로 된 거야. 적어도 지금은.’
162|
163|내가 언제부터 앞날을 내려다보며 살았었나. 그날 하루, 그 순간에 따라 걸어가야 할 길을 선택했고 여기까지 왔다.
164|
165|그리고 오늘 내가 택한 길은, 여름철 백사장처럼 넓고 따뜻했다.
166|
167|
168|
169|* * *
170|
171|
172|
173|전에 TV에서 봤다. 운동선수들은 각자만의 루틴이 있다고.
174|
175|어떤 축구 선수는 경기장에 들어설 때 왼발부터 내디디고, 메이저리그 간판 타자는 한 번 배트를 휘두를 때마다 해바라기 씨를 뱉는다고 했다.
176|
177|평범한 사람의 시선에는 그게 뭐 대단한 의식이라고 유난을 떠나 싶겠지만, 사실 마음의 안정과 행운에 대한 미신은 누구나 갖고 있는 거다.
178|
179|그리고 이런 루틴과 미신에 대해 누구보다 철두철미한 직업이 바로 헌터다.
180|
181|축구 경기에서 져도 하늘이 무너지지는 않는다. 역전 만루 찬스에서 삼 구 삼진을 당한다고 해서 땅이 꺼지지는 않는다.
182|
183|하지만 헌터는 운이 없으면 바로 골로 간다.
184|
185|그들에게는 다음 경기도, 다음 타석도 없다. 그저 숨이 끊기기 직전 자신의 일생과 가족들의 얼굴을 떠올리며, 문득 생각할 뿐이다.
186|
187|‘시발, 오늘은 파란 팬티를 입었어야 했는데.’
188|
189|농담 같지만 실화다. 몇 년 전 한창 인기를 끌다가 게이트에서 죽은 어느 A급 헌터의 마지막 유언이기도 했다.
190|
191|‘아니, 빨간 팬티였나?’
192|
193|정신없이 일만 하던 시절이라 기억이 가물가물한데, 아무튼.
194|
195|이 이야기에서 중요한 것은 나 역시 지금껏 철두철미하게 지켜 온 나만의 루틴이 있고, 지금 막 그 루틴이 깨졌다는 거다.
196|
197|쾅!
198|
199|마치 폭발하듯 열리는 문.
200|
201|만일의 경우를 대비하여 걸어 두었던 잠금장치가 박살 났고, 다행히 그보다 한발 앞서 모든 대비를 끝마친 나는 애써 침착하게 불청객을 맞이했다.
202|
203|“어허, 이제는 노크도 안 하시고 막 들어오시네.”
204|
205|후욱. 훅.
206|
207|거친 숨결과 이마에 맺힌 땀. 흐트러진 정장 차림을 한 불청객을 바라보며, 나는 말을 이었다.
208|
209|“최 팀장님.”
210|
211|평소였다면 반가운 얼굴이었겠지만, 지금만큼은 저 잘생긴 얼굴에 한 방 먹여 주고 싶은 충동이 든다.
212|
213|하지만 이제는 명실공히 길드장이라고 불려야 할 최 팀장은 내 불편한 심기를 눈치채지 못했다.
214|
215|아니, 그럴 겨를조차 없다고 해야 더 옳았다.
216|
217|“훅. 후욱.”
218|
219|뭐 마왕한테 쫓기기라도 했나.
220|
221|이제 중원의 여느 절정 고수와 비교해도 꿀리지 않는 최 팀장은 겨우겨우 호흡을 가다듬더니, 손에 든 것을 불쑥 내밀며 외쳤다.
222|
223|“이거, 이거 도대체 뭡니까!”
224|
225|“볼일 없으면 좀 이따가…… 아. 그거요?”
226|
227|“그거요라니. 그거요라니! 그렇게 쉽게 말해도 되는 문젭니까, 이게!”
228|
229|발작 버튼 ON.
230|
231|대수롭지 않은 내 반문에 거의 자지러지는 최 팀장의 모습에, 나는 어쩔 수 없이 헌터 훈련소를 수료한 이래 단 하루도 거르지 않고 지켜 온 필수 루틴을 깨트려야 한다는 것을 깨달았다.
232|
233|그리고 지금 당장 저 ‘물건’에 대한 설명을 피할 수 없다는 것 역시도.
234|
235|“진정하세요, 진정. 다 말씀드릴 테니까 우선 그것부터 내려놓으시고. 아, 마실 거는 뭘로?”
236|
237|“진태경 씨. 지금 뭘 마시는 게 중요한 게 아니잖습…….”
238|
239|“그냥 커피 드릴게요. 그 뭐냐. 지난번에 사무실 생긴 기념으로 선물해 주셨던 호랑이 똥 커피로.”
240|
241|“허.”
242|
243|“괜찮죠?”
244|
245|경악과 황당함이 뒤섞인 눈으로 나를 바라보던 최 팀장이 무너지듯 소파에 주저앉았다.
246|
247|파르르 떨리는 그의 손에는 한 뭉텅이의 종이와, 내 손으로 직접 써 내려간 글씨가 적혀 있었다.
248|
249|[싱글벙글 마나 연공법]
250|
251|다시 봐도 명필이다.
252|
253|
254|
255|* * *
256|
257|
258|
259|최 팀장은 확실히 있는 집 도련님이었다.
260|
261|조금 전까지는 뿔이 뽑힌 미노타우로스처럼 씩씩거리더니, 진한 커피 향을 맡은 것만으로도 침착함을 되찾는 그의 모습에 나도 괜히 코를 킁킁거렸다.
262|
263|“호랑이 똥 커피에 심신 안정, 뭐 그런 효능이 있나 봐요? 아니면 그냥 최 팀장님 루틴 같은 건가?”
264|
265|최 팀장이 내 궁금증을 냉정한 목소리로 해결해주었다.
266|
267|“호랑이가 아니라 고양이입니다. 사향 고양이요.”
268|
269|“호랑이나 고양이나, 어쨌든.”
270|
271|“그리고 똥보다는 변으로 하시죠. 분비물이라는 단어도 있습니다.”
272|
273|“똥.”
274|
275|“변. 아니면 분비물.”
276|
277|“예. 그러니까 똥.”
278|
279|“잊으셨나 본데, 이제 곧 저녁 시간입니다. 그렇게 사람 면전에 대고 자꾸 똥이라고 하시면…….”
280|
281|“똥.”
282|
283|“…….”
284|
285|점점 변 같아지는 분위기 속, 먼저 뒤로 물러난 것은 최 팀장이었다.
286|
287|“좋습니다. 지금은 그게 중요한 게 아니니까요.”
288|
289|“음.”
290|
291|다시 생각해 보니 병신 같다.
292|
293|마음 깊이 반성한 나는 날카롭게 날 선 마음을 가라앉혔다.
294|
295|최 팀장 때문에 반드시 지켜야 하는 필수 루틴이 깨지긴 했지만, 따지고 보면 그 원인 제공도 내가 직접 한 셈이니까.
296|
297|[싱글벙글 마나 연공법]
298|
299|애초에 이런 걸 본 이상, 최 팀장이 아니라 그 누구든 한걸음에 달려왔을 것이다. 설령 그 사람이 미국 대통령이라 해도 그 사실은 달라지지 않는다.
300|
301|“사안이 사안인 만큼, 단도직입적으로 묻겠습니다.”
302|
303|살짝 떨리는 목소리. 최 팀장이 나를 응시하며 천천히 말을 이었다.
304|
305|“이것…… 아니, 이 마나 연공법. 출처가 어떻게 됩니까?”
306|
307|나는 망설임 없이 대답했다.
308|
309|“누구겠어요. 지금 최 팀장님이랑 마주 보고 있는 사람이지.”
310|
311|“……!”
312|
313|“제가 직접 만들었습니다. 처음부터 끝까지.”
314|
315|순간 내려앉은 숨 막히는 침묵. 흔들리는 눈동자로 말없이 나를 바라보던 최 팀장이 참았던 숨을 토해 냈다.
316|

Normally, I’d have been glad to see him. Right now, I wanted to punch that handsome face.

[P79]
But Team Leader Choi—who, by all rights, should now be called the Guild Master—didn’t notice my mood. Or rather, he had no attention to spare for it.

[P80]
“Huff. Hoo.”

[P81]
*What, was the Demon King chasing him?*

[P82]
These days, Team Leader Choi could hold his own against any Peak master in the Central Plains. He finally caught his breath, thrust out what he was holding, and shouted, “What is this? What on earth is this?”

[P83]
“If it can wait, come back a little later… Oh. That?”

[P84]
“*That?* Is this something you can dismiss with ‘that’?”

[P85]
Rage button: ON.

[P86]

[P87]
“Calm down. I’ll tell you everything. Just put that down first. Oh, what would you like to drink?”

[P88]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, what I drink is hardly the important thing right n—”

[P89]
“I’ll make you coffee. That tiger-poop coffee you gave me to celebrate the new office.”

[P90]
“Hah.”

[P91]
“That okay?”

[P92]
Team Leader Choi stared at me, shock and disbelief mingling in his eyes, then sank onto the sofa.

[P93]
In his trembling hand was a sheaf of papers covered in my own handwriting.

[P94]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P95]
Looking at it again, my penmanship was a work of art.

[P96]
* * *

[P97]
Team Leader Choi really was a rich kid.

[P98]
A moment ago, he’d been snorting like a Minotaur with its horns ripped out. One whiff of rich coffee, though, and he had his composure back. I couldn’t help sniffing the air myself.

[P99]
“Does tiger-poop coffee calm you down or something? Or is this one of your routines?”

[P100]
Team Leader Choi answered coolly. “It isn’t a tiger. It’s a cat. A civet cat.”

[P101]
“Tiger, cat. Whatever.”

[P102]
“And could you say ‘feces’ instead of ‘poop’? ‘Excrement’ would also do.”

[P103]
“Poop.”

[P104]
“Feces. Or excrement.”

[P105]
“Right. So, poop.”

[P106]
“In case you’ve forgotten, it’s almost dinnertime. If you keep saying ‘poop’ to my face…”

[P107]
“Poop.”

[P108]
“…”

[P109]
As the atmosphere grew increasingly shitty, Team Leader Choi was the first to back down.

[P110]
“Fine. That isn’t what matters right now.”

[P111]
“Mm.”

[P112]
On second thought, I was being an idiot. I took a breath and let go of my irritation. Team Leader Choi had broken a routine I absolutely needed to keep, but I was the one who’d given him the reason.

[P113]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P114]
Anyone who saw this would have come running. Even the President of the United States.

[P115]
“Given what’s at stake, I’ll ask you directly.”

[P116]
His voice trembled slightly. He looked me in the eye and went on.

[P117]
“This… no, this mana cultivation method. Where did it come from?”

[P118]
I answered without hesitation.

[P119]
“Who do you think? The person sitting across from you.”

[P120]
“…!”

[P121]
“I made it myself. From beginning to end.”

[P122]
A suffocating silence fell. Team Leader Choi stared at me, eyes wavering, before letting out the breath he’d been holding.

[P123]
“Hoo.”

[P124]
“Why are you so surprised? Didn’t the errand boy I sent explain?”

[P125]
Of course, he wasn’t just an errand boy. The Skeleton King might be a little unhinged, but he was a powerful named monster—and secretly operated as an S-rank Hunter for the Peace Guild.

[P126]
*More importantly, I could trust him.*

[P127]
Team Leader Choi knew that better than anyone. He gave a quiet laugh.

[P128]
“That was quite an errand boy.”

[P129]
“That’s why I gave it to him. I meant to hand it to you myself, but you weren’t there.”

[P130]
“…I had somewhere to stop by.”

[P131]
He left it at that, and I didn’t ask where he’d been.

[P132]
Two months had passed since someone had suddenly left us all. Warmth still lingered in the space they’d left behind, like the cup of coffee Team Leader Choi hadn’t touched.

[P133]
“I heard what you told Skeleton King. No—Mr. King. But I’m sorry…”

[P134]
“You had to check for yourself. I get it.”

[P135]
“Yes. Though the moment I looked inside, before anyone explained a thing, I was certain. You’re the only person in the world who could make a mana cultivation method like this.”

[P136]
At his praise, I scratched the back of my head.

[P137]
“Come on, it’s not *that* impressive. I did put a lot of thought and effort into making it something even beginners could learn, but…”

[P138]
“There can’t be many S-rank Hunters with handwriting this bad. Or people with a sense for names like yours.”

[P139]
“What?”

[P140]
“And someone who has both? I didn’t need to think twice.”

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
“That’s how I knew this mana cultivation method could only have come from one person: Jin Taekyung.”

[P143]
“…”

[P144]
I looked from Team Leader Choi’s utterly certain face to **[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]** on the table, then back again.

[P145]
*What the fuck.*

[P146]
Mana cultivation method or not, maybe I should just tear the whole thing to shreds.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. “Shanxi Province is some distance from the Central Plains, yes. But what does that have to do with your secret…?”

[P22]
“Farther than that. Farther than Nanman, even.”

[P23]
“Farther than Nanman?”

[P24]
“Yes. So far you couldn’t reach it if you walked your entire life.”

[P25]
“You mean you have to take a boat?”

[P26]
“No. That’s not it. I mean… it’s a completely different world.”

[P27]
A completely different world.

[P28]
Jeok Cheongang listened to what came next, then fell silent for a long time, trying to make sense of it in his own way.

[P29]
“So you’re saying you came from the realm of immortals.”

[P30]
“…Uh. I guess you could put it that way.”

[P31]
“Are you a Little Immortal?”

[P32]
“I’m an ordinary citizen.”

[P33]
If Jeok Cheongang had been from the modern world, we might have understood each other a little better. In a world that already had monsters and magic, one man from Murim wouldn’t have been impossible to comprehend.

[P34]
Whether that man wound up in a psychiatric hospital or got dragged off to a laboratory afterward was another question.

[P35]
But Jeok Cheongang had spent over a hundred years in Murim, a world without even the internet. Everything I told him was bound to sound bewildering.

[P36]
“When you fall asleep here, you go to the realm of immortals?”

[P37]
“Not every time, but unless something unusual happens, yes.”

[P38]
“And when you wish to leave the realm of immortals and return here…”

[P39]
“It works the same way. Each time, time in the other world moves very slowly.”

[P40]
“…Goddamn it.”

[P41]
After a desperate struggle to hold on to his common sense and reason, Jeok Cheongang finally reached a conclusion.

[P42]
“Damn it. I don’t know.”

[P43]
“What?”

[P44]
“I’m telling you, I still don’t understand.”

[P45]
Some truths couldn’t be understood even if you saw them with your own eyes and heard them with your own ears. Everything I’d told Jeok Cheongang was like that for him.

[P46]
Yet amid all his confusion, one thing remained unchanged.

[P47]
“But the idiot standing before this old man is named Jin Taekyung. Not a Little Immortal descended from the realm of immortals. Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”

[P48]
“…!”

[P49]
“That alone is enough.”

[P50]
I hadn’t understood then why those words left me speechless. Why I had to clench my teeth against the heat rising in my chest.

[P51]
But… yes. As Jeok Cheongang had said, that alone was enough for me, too.

[P52]
And now I thought I understood why.

[P53]
I’d been afraid. Afraid that the other world, now such a large part of my life, might deny that I belonged there.

[P54]
*What am I, a little kid?*

[P55]
A rueful laugh slipped out. At the same time, the weight pressing on my heart lifted, and I felt relieved.

[P56]
*Right. This is enough. For now, at least.*

[P57]
Since when had I ever lived with my eyes fixed on the future? I’d chosen where to go one day, one moment at a time, and that had brought me here.

[P58]
The path I’d chosen today was as wide and warm as a beach in summer.

[P59]
* * *

[P60]
I’d seen on TV that athletes all had their own routines.

[P61]
One soccer player always stepped onto the field with his left foot first. A star Major League batter spat out a sunflower seed every time he swung his bat.

[P62]
To an ordinary person, that might seem like an awful lot of fuss over nothing. But everyone had little superstitions for peace of mind and good luck.

[P63]
No profession took them more seriously than Hunters.

[P64]
Lose a soccer game, and the sky doesn’t fall. Strike out on three pitches with the bases loaded and a chance to take the lead, and the ground doesn’t open beneath you.

[P65]
A Hunter, though, could be dead the moment luck turned bad.

[P66]
There was no next game. No next at-bat. Just their life and their family’s faces flashing through their mind as they drew their final breath, and one sudden thought:

[P67]
*Fuck, I should’ve worn my blue underwear today.*

[P68]
It sounded like a joke, but it was true. Those had been the last words of an A-rank Hunter who’d died in a Gate a few years ago, at the height of his popularity.

[P69]
*Or was it red underwear?*

[P70]
I’d been working nonstop back then, so the details were hazy. Anyway.

[P71]
The point was, I had a routine of my own. I’d followed it without fail until now, and it had just been broken.

[P72]
*Bang!*

[P73]
The door flew open as if something had exploded.

[P74]
The lock I’d installed as a precaution shattered. Fortunately, I’d finished all my preparations just in time. I did my best to greet the uninvited guest calmly.

[P75]
“Well, well. You don’t even knock anymore?”

[P76]
“Huff. Hah.”

[P77]
He was breathing hard, sweat beading on his forehead, his suit in disarray. I looked at him and added, “Team Leader Choi.”

[P78]
Normally, I’d have been glad to see him. Right now, I wanted to punch that handsome face.

[P79]
But Team Leader Choi—who, by all rights, should now be called the Guild Master—didn’t notice my mood. Or rather, he had no attention to spare for it.

[P80]
“Huff. Hoo.”

[P81]
*What, was the Demon King chasing him?*

[P82]
These days, Team Leader Choi could hold his own against any Peak master in the Central Plains. He finally caught his breath, thrust out what he was holding, and shouted, “What is this? What on earth is this?”

[P83]
“If it can wait, come back a little later… Oh. That?”

[P84]
“*That?* Is this something you can dismiss with ‘that’?”

[P85]
Rage button: ON.

[P86]
The way he nearly lost his mind over my casual answer told me two things. First, I was going to have to break the essential routine I’d followed every day since finishing Hunter training. Second, there was no getting out of explaining that *thing* right now.

[P87]
“Calm down. I’ll tell you everything. Just put that down first. Oh, what would you like to drink?”

[P88]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, what I drink is hardly the important thing right n—”

[P89]
“I’ll make you coffee. That tiger-poop coffee you gave me to celebrate the new office.”

[P90]
“Hah.”

[P91]
“That okay?”

[P92]
Team Leader Choi stared at me, shock and disbelief mingling in his eyes, then sank onto the sofa.

[P93]
In his trembling hand was a sheaf of papers covered in my own handwriting.

[P94]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P95]
Looking at it again, my penmanship was a work of art.

[P96]
* * *

[P97]
Team Leader Choi really was a rich kid.

[P98]
A moment ago, he’d been snorting like a Minotaur with its horns ripped out. One whiff of rich coffee, though, and he had his composure back. I couldn’t help sniffing the air myself.

[P99]
“Does tiger-poop coffee calm you down or something? Or is this one of your routines?”

[P100]
Team Leader Choi answered coolly. “It isn’t a tiger. It’s a cat. A civet cat.”

[P101]
“Tiger, cat. Whatever.”

[P102]
“And could you say ‘feces’ instead of ‘poop’? ‘Excrement’ would also do.”

[P103]
“Poop.”

[P104]
“Feces. Or excrement.”

[P105]
“Right. So, poop.”

[P106]
“In case you’ve forgotten, it’s almost dinnertime. If you keep saying ‘poop’ to my face…”

[P107]
“Poop.”

[P108]
“…”

[P109]
As the atmosphere grew increasingly shitty, Team Leader Choi was the first to back down.

[P110]
“Fine. That isn’t what matters right now.”

[P111]
“Mm.”

[P112]
On second thought, I was being an idiot. I took a breath and let go of my irritation. Team Leader Choi had broken a routine I absolutely needed to keep, but I was the one who’d given him the reason.

[P113]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P114]
Anyone who saw this would have come running. Even the President of the United States.

[P115]
“Given what’s at stake, I’ll ask you directly.”

[P116]
His voice trembled slightly. He looked me in the eye and went on.

[P117]
“This… no, this mana cultivation method. Where did it come from?”

[P118]
I answered without hesitation.

[P119]
“Who do you think? The person sitting across from you.”

[P120]
“…!”

[P121]
“I made it myself. From beginning to end.”

[P122]
A suffocating silence fell. Team Leader Choi stared at me, eyes wavering, before letting out the breath he’d been holding.

[P123]
“Hoo.”

[P124]
“Why are you so surprised? Didn’t the errand boy I sent explain?”

[P125]
Of course, he wasn’t just an errand boy. The Skeleton King might be a little unhinged, but he was a powerful named monster—and secretly operated as an S-rank Hunter for the Peace Guild.

[P126]
*More importantly, I could trust him.*

[P127]
Team Leader Choi knew that better than anyone. He gave a quiet laugh.

[P128]
“That was quite an errand boy.”

[P129]
“That’s why I gave it to him. I meant to hand it to you myself, but you weren’t there.”

[P130]
“…I had somewhere to stop by.”

[P131]
He left it at that, and I didn’t ask where he’d been.

[P132]
Two months had passed since someone had suddenly left us all. Warmth still lingered in the space they’d left behind, like the cup of coffee Team Leader Choi hadn’t touched.

[P133]
“I heard what you told Skeleton King. No—Mr. King. But I’m sorry…”

[P134]
“You had to check for yourself. I get it.”

[P135]
“Yes. Though the moment I looked inside, before anyone explained a thing, I was certain. You’re the only person in the world who could make a mana cultivation method like this.”

[P136]
At his praise, I scratched the back of my head.

[P137]
“Come on, it’s not *that* impressive. I did put a lot of thought and effort into making it something even beginners could learn, but…”

[P138]
“There can’t be many S-rank Hunters with handwriting this bad. Or people with a sense for names like yours.”

[P139]
“What?”

[P140]
“And someone who has both? I didn’t need to think twice.”

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
“That’s how I knew this mana cultivation method could only have come from one person: Jin Taekyung.”

[P143]
“…”

[P144]
I looked from Team Leader Choi’s utterly certain face to **[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]** on the table, then back again.

[P145]
*What the fuck.*

[P146]
Mana cultivation method or not, maybe I should just tear the whole thing to shreds.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

If Jeok Cheongang had been from the modern world, we might have understood each other a little better. In a world that already had monsters and magic, one man from Murim wouldn’t have been impossible to comprehend.

[P34]
Whether that man wound up in a psychiatric hospital or got dragged off to a laboratory afterward was another question.

[P35]
But Jeok Cheongang had spent over a hundred years in Murim, a world without even the internet. Everything I told him was bound to sound bewildering.

[P36]
“When you fall asleep here, you go to the realm of immortals?”

[P37]
“Not every time, but unless something unusual happens, yes.”

[P38]
“And when you wish to leave the realm of immortals and return here…”

[P39]
“It works the same way. Each time, time in the other world moves very slowly.”

[P40]
“…Goddamn it.”

[P41]
After a desperate struggle to hold on to his common sense and reason, Jeok Cheongang finally reached a conclusion.

[P42]
“Damn it. I don’t know.”

[P43]
“What?”

[P44]
“I’m telling you, I still don’t understand.”

[P45]
Some truths couldn’t be understood even if you saw them with your own eyes and heard them with your own ears. Everything I’d told Jeok Cheongang was like that for him.

[P46]
Yet amid all his confusion, one thing remained unchanged.

[P47]
“But the idiot standing before this old man is named Jin Taekyung. Not a Little Immortal descended from the realm of immortals. Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”

[P48]
“…!”

[P49]
“That alone is enough.”

[P50]
I hadn’t understood then why those words left me speechless. Why I had to clench my teeth against the heat rising in my chest.

[P51]
But… yes. As Jeok Cheongang had said, that alone was enough for me, too.

[P52]
And now I thought I understood why.

[P53]
I’d been afraid. Afraid that the other world, now such a large part of my life, might deny that I belonged there.

[P54]
*What am I, a little kid?*

[P55]
A rueful laugh slipped out. At the same time, the weight pressing on my heart lifted, and I felt relieved.

[P56]
*Right. This is enough. For now, at least.*

[P57]
Since when had I ever lived with my eyes fixed on the future? I’d chosen where to go one day, one moment at a time, and that had brought me here.

[P58]
The path I’d chosen today was as wide and warm as a beach in summer.

[P59]
* * *

[P60]
I’d seen on TV that athletes all had their own routines.

[P61]
One soccer player always stepped onto the field with his left foot first. A star Major League batter spat out a sunflower seed every time he swung his bat.

[P62]
To an ordinary person, that might seem like an awful lot of fuss over nothing. But everyone had little superstitions for peace of mind and good luck.

[P63]
No profession took them more seriously than Hunters.

[P64]
Lose a soccer game, and the sky doesn’t fall. Strike out on three pitches with the bases loaded and a chance to take the lead, and the ground doesn’t open beneath you.

[P65]
A Hunter, though, could be dead the moment luck turned bad.

[P66]
There was no next game. No next at-bat. Just their life and their family’s faces flashing through their mind as they drew their final breath, and one sudden thought:

[P67]
*Fuck, I should’ve worn my blue underwear today.*

[P68]
It sounded like a joke, but it was true. Those had been the last words of an A-rank Hunter who’d died in a Gate a few years ago, at the height of his popularity.

[P69]
*Or was it red underwear?*

[P70]
I’d been working nonstop back then, so the details were hazy. Anyway.

[P71]
The point was, I had a routine of my own. I’d followed it without fail until now, and it had just been broken.

[P72]
*Bang!*

[P73]
The door flew open as if something had exploded.

[P74]
The lock I’d installed as a precaution shattered. Fortunately, I’d finished all my preparations just in time. I did my best to greet the uninvited guest calmly.

[P75]
“Well, well. You don’t even knock anymore?”

[P76]
“Huff. Hah.”

[P77]
He was breathing hard, sweat beading on his forehead, his suit in disarray. I looked at him and added, “Team Leader Choi.”

[P78]
Normally, I’d have been glad to see him. Right now, I wanted to punch that handsome face.

[P79]
But Team Leader Choi—who, by all rights, should now be called the Guild Master—didn’t notice my mood. Or rather, he had no attention to spare for it.

[P80]
“Huff. Hoo.”

[P81]
*What, was the Demon King chasing him?*

[P82]
These days, Team Leader Choi could hold his own against any Peak master in the Central Plains. He finally caught his breath, thrust out what he was holding, and shouted, “What is this? What on earth is this?”

[P83]
“If it can wait, come back a little later… Oh. That?”

[P84]
“*That?* Is this something you can dismiss with ‘that’?”

[P85]
Rage button: ON.

[P86]
The way he nearly lost his mind over my casual answer told me two things. First, I was going to have to break the essential routine I’d followed every day since finishing Hunter training. Second, there was no getting out of explaining that *thing* right now.

[P87]
“Calm down. I’ll tell you everything. Just put that down first. Oh, what would you like to drink?”

[P88]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, what I drink is hardly the important thing right n—”

[P89]
“I’ll make you coffee. That tiger-poop coffee you gave me to celebrate the new office.”

[P90]
“Hah.”

[P91]
“That okay?”

[P92]
Team Leader Choi stared at me, shock and disbelief mingling in his eyes, then sank onto the sofa.

[P93]
In his trembling hand was a sheaf of papers covered in my own handwriting.

[P94]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P95]
Looking at it again, my penmanship was a work of art.

[P96]
* * *

[P97]
Team Leader Choi really was a rich kid.

[P98]
A moment ago, he’d been snorting like a Minotaur with its horns ripped out. One whiff of rich coffee, though, and he had his composure back. I couldn’t help sniffing the air myself.

[P99]
“Does tiger-poop coffee calm you down or something? Or is this one of your routines?”

[P100]
Team Leader Choi answered coolly. “It isn’t a tiger. It’s a cat. A civet cat.”

[P101]
“Tiger, cat. Whatever.”

[P102]
“And could you say ‘feces’ instead of ‘poop’? ‘Excrement’ would also do.”

[P103]
“Poop.”

[P104]
“Feces. Or excrement.”

[P105]
“Right. So, poop.”

[P106]
“In case you’ve forgotten, it’s almost dinnertime. If you keep saying ‘poop’ to my face…”

[P107]
“Poop.”

[P108]
“…”

[P109]
As the atmosphere grew increasingly shitty, Team Leader Choi was the first to back down.

[P110]
“Fine. That isn’t what matters right now.”

[P111]
“Mm.”

[P112]
On second thought, I was being an idiot. I took a breath and let go of my irritation. Team Leader Choi had broken a routine I absolutely needed to keep, but I was the one who’d given him the reason.

[P113]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P114]
Anyone who saw this would have come running. Even the President of the United States.

[P115]
“Given what’s at stake, I’ll ask you directly.”

[P116]
His voice trembled slightly. He looked me in the eye and went on.

[P117]
“This… no, this mana cultivation method. Where did it come from?”

[P118]
I answered without hesitation.

[P119]
“Who do you think? The person sitting across from you.”

[P120]
“…!”

[P121]
“I made it myself. From beginning to end.”

[P122]
A suffocating silence fell. Team Leader Choi stared at me, eyes wavering, before letting out the breath he’d been holding.

[P123]
“Hoo.”

[P124]
“Why are you so surprised? Didn’t the errand boy I sent explain?”

[P125]
Of course, he wasn’t just an errand boy. The Skeleton King might be a little unhinged, but he was a powerful named monster—and secretly operated as an S-rank Hunter for the Peace Guild.

[P126]
*More importantly, I could trust him.*

[P127]
Team Leader Choi knew that better than anyone. He gave a quiet laugh.

[P128]
“That was quite an errand boy.”

[P129]
“That’s why I gave it to him. I meant to hand it to you myself, but you weren’t there.”

[P130]
“…I had somewhere to stop by.”

[P131]
He left it at that, and I didn’t ask where he’d been.

[P132]
Two months had passed since someone had suddenly left us all. Warmth still lingered in the space they’d left behind, like the cup of coffee Team Leader Choi hadn’t touched.

[P133]
“I heard what you told Skeleton King. No—Mr. King. But I’m sorry…”

[P134]
“You had to check for yourself. I get it.”

[P135]
“Yes. Though the moment I looked inside, before anyone explained a thing, I was certain. You’re the only person in the world who could make a mana cultivation method like this.”

[P136]
At his praise, I scratched the back of my head.

[P137]
“Come on, it’s not *that* impressive. I did put a lot of thought and effort into making it something even beginners could learn, but…”

[P138]
“There can’t be many S-rank Hunters with handwriting this bad. Or people with a sense for names like yours.”

[P139]
“What?”

[P140]
“And someone who has both? I didn’t need to think twice.”

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
“That’s how I knew this mana cultivation method could only have come from one person: Jin Taekyung.”

[P143]
“…”

[P144]
I looked from Team Leader Choi’s utterly certain face to **[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]** on the table, then back again.

[P145]
*What the fuck.*

[P146]
Mana cultivation method or not, maybe I should just tear the whole thing to shreds.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
